objectClass.primaryType: open-air votive shrine pavilion (Thai/Hindu san phra phrom, Erawan type)
motionPotential: static landmark geometry - no articulated parts, no moving assemblies
objectClass.notes: 4-fold radial symmetry about the vertical axis carries the architecture and is the honest way to fill the three unseen sides. Symmetry is broken only by the deity, which faces one direction, and by two offering trays on one edge. The seated four-faced figure is a gilded STATUE, not a living figure: sculpted geometry, no anatomy gates. Deliberately not a Buddha image. The pavilion is OPEN on all four sides - that openness is the identity, since the deity must read from the street on every approach.

reasoning: repetitionDensity 9: ~48 elephant figurines, ~40 turned balusters, 4 columns, 4 hip ridge caps and 6 garland loops are 102 of the ~110 visible parts. Every one of them must be an InstancedMesh or the draw-call and geometry ceilings are unreachable.

actionReadinessNeed 1: static landmark geometry, one root pivot, no sockets, no destruction groups.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Repetition systems are not optional here: they are the only way 102 repeated parts fit inside 12 unique geometries. Action-ready hierarchy is NOT needed - the prop has no moving parts, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct answer, not a gap. The model must still be explodable and clickable.

Four faces on a single head block at 90-degree intervals under a tiered pointed crown. Only the front face and part of one side face are legible.
Four gilt strips capping the roof hips from eave corner to apex, plus a gilt band along the eave edge. This is what reads the roof as gilded Thai architecture rather than a plain shingle pyramid.

Horizontal plank courses running the full width of each roof slope, ~16 courses per slope, each standing slightly proud of the one above. Built as geometry via micro-steps in the lathe profile, NOT as a texture.

The roof slope is not straight: it flares concavely near the eave, so the last third of the slope turns outward and down. A straight cone passes a silhouette IoU test here, so this needs the swept-arc treatment.
Turned hardwood balusters with a vase/bead profile - narrow neck, swelling belly, narrow foot - set between the top and bottom rails with clear gaps, so the balustrade is see-through.
Vertical fluting on the collar at the top of each gilt column, and a plain torus ring at each column base.
The granite cap slab overhangs the plinth base on all four sides and its lower edge is chamfered, throwing the shadow line that separates podium from base.

Fine high-frequency light/dark feldspar flake across plinth, cap slab, deck and pedestal. This is what separates granite from grey concrete and is the one material on the prop that may earn a texture.
Low-saturation ochre and brown wax runs and offering residue streaking the deck slab, heaviest near the rail and the offering trays.
Gilt axial spire at the roof apex: a stepped base, a swelling bulb, a tapering needle and a small ball terminal.

preSpecAssessment.unknownsNote: Empty because every item was DECIDED, not because none existed. Seven single-view unknowns were carried through intake; each is filled by a stated assumption at a stated confidence and each is preserved verbatim in resolvedUnknowns and in `assumptions`. Four of them -- the three hidden elevations, the three hidden faces of the figure, the arms the plate hides behind garlands, and whether the balustrade has a gate -- cannot be closed from one plate at all. More views is the only thing that would close them, and this asset ships one plate by design.
resolvedUnknowns: Rear and both lateral elevations are unseen in the single plate; filled from the 4-fold radial symmetry the visible corner establishes (confidence 0.8).
The three non-front faces of the four-faced figure are unseen; built as four copies of the legible front face at 90 degree intervals, which is what the iconography prescribes (confidence 0.45).

The deity's arm count and mudras are occluded by the garland masses in the plate, so there is no evidence for them; the arms are NOT modelled (confidence 0.3). The garlands themselves were removed from the build after review -- displaced spheres read as orange blobs rather than flowers -- so the omission is no longer masked.
Whether the balustrade has an approach gate is not visible; built as a continuous closed ring on all four sides (confidence 0.35).
Exact baluster count per side: 16 legible on the near side at consistent spacing; built as 10 per side, 40 total, to hold the triangle budget while keeping the see-through rhythm (confidence 0.6).
Exact elephant figurine count: ~12 per side legible across the two visible sides; built as 12 per side, 48 total (confidence 0.65).
The plinth underside is never seen on a ground-standing prop and is not modelled.

The counter reads componentTree only, and four of this prop's meso assemblies -- 40 balusters, 48 elephant figurines, 4 columns, and 4 hip ridge caps, 96 parts in all -- live in repetitionSystems, which it does not look at. staticProp.note: This shrine has NO moving parts. It ships ONE pivot -- the generator's own root Group at base-center -- and ZERO sockets. A named pivot promises a part turns on that axis and a named socket promises something attaches there; neither is true of any part of a masonry and timber shrine. Declaring a pivot per component would describe a machine that does not exist. The model is still explodable and clickable: every component and cluster is a named node under the root.

componentTree.name: Granite podium: plinth, cap slab, deck and deity pedestal
componentTree.topologyRationale: A single square solid of revolution. LatheGeometry at segments=4 puts the profile radius at the CORNERS, so a face half-width he is authored as r = he*sqrt(2) and the component is rotated 45 deg about Y to bring the faces axis-aligned. One profile therefore carries four stacked masses that would otherwise be four boxes, four draw calls and four geometries.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Profile from the ground: plinth base block to y=0.92, chamfered cap slab flaring to the full 5.00 m width, the exposed cap-slab annulus at y=1.20 that the elephant ring stands on, the deck slab, the deck top, then the stepped deity pedestal closing with a flat cap at y=2.00.
geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: 15 profile points at 4 segments: 112 triangles for the entire stone mass.
geometryDescriptor.coplanarNote: Nothing is authored flush against this component. The rails sink 0.04 m below the deck top, the columns sink 0.02 m, and every elephant instance is embedded 0.015 m into the cap ledge, so no co-facing pair shares a plane.

destruction.notes: Static landmark geometry; the asset declares no destruction groups, so no component carries a fractureGroup.

collider.notes: One box around the WHOLE prop envelope, as the asset declares -- it is hung on the podium because that is the component that spans the footprint, not because the box stops at the podium. The elephant figurines deliberately get no collider of their own: a physics proxy per votive object costs more to test than the prop is worth, and nothing in an FPS needs to collide with an individual figurine.

localFeatures.description: 0.04 m chamfer under and over the cap slab, throwing the shadow line that separates podium from base.
The exposed cap-slab annulus at y=1.20 between he 2.02 and 2.46, which the 48 elephant instances stand on, each embedded 0.015 m.
The four points on the deck top at he 1.62 where the gilt columns sink 0.02 m in, so no column base is flush with the deck.

colorMaterialRecipe.notes: Flat de-lit mid-grey granite; speckle deliberately not textured -- see materials.granite.textureless.

surfaceDetail.notes: Flat sawn granite faces with a 0.04 m chamfer under and over the cap slab. The feldspar speckle measured at heightP90Gradient 0.07194 is deliberately NOT built: it resolves at ~0.003 m, which is under a pixel at prop distance. bumpAmplitude 0 is honest -- there is no relief on this surface beyond the chamfers, which are silhouette, not bump.

componentTree.name: Concave-flared hip roof with timber fascia band
componentTree.topologyRationale: The second square solid of revolution. A closed profile - up the outer slope, over the apex, back down an inner surface inset by the 0.10 m shell thickness - so the roof is a real shell with a visible underside rather than a one-sided cone that shows backfaces from the street.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Fascia band from the column tops at y=3.52 to y=3.90, an eave lip turned out and down at y=3.96 and he=2.29, then the slope to the apex at y=5.30. The slope is a straight pitch plus a concave kick that dies out by the first quarter, which is what reads as a Thai hip roof rather than a shingle pyramid. Sixteen plank courses are micro-steps of 0.022 m in the profile: the coursing is GEOMETRY, which is what lets the timber material stay textureless.
geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: 70 profile points at 4 segments: 552 triangles, of which about 256 are the plank coursing.
geometryDescriptor.swept_arc_note: The concave kick is the curve claim on this prop. A straight cone occupies roughly the right silhouette cells and would pass an IoU test, so this needs swept_arc_gate.py rather than a silhouette score.

destruction.notes: Static landmark geometry; the asset declares no destruction groups, so no component carries a fractureGroup.

localFeatures.description: Sixteen 0.022 m micro-steps in the lathe profile, one per plank course at a 0.084 m pitch. Geometry, which is what lets the timber material stay textureless.
The concave kick over the last quarter of the slope, from a straight pitch outward and down to an eave lip at he 2.29. This is the curve claim on the prop.
The four hip lines from eave corner to apex that the gilt ridge caps sit on, standing 0.03 m proud so they are never coplanar with the roof surface.

colorMaterialRecipe.notes: Dark stained hardwood; the plank relief is geometry, not albedo.

surfaceDetail.notes: Sixteen plank courses at a 0.084 m pitch, each standing 0.022 m proud of the one above, built as micro-steps in the lathe profile. This is the prop's largest piece of surface relief and it is GEOMETRY: it casts real silhouette against the sky at the eave, which a normal map cannot.

componentTree.name: Gilt axial spire finial
componentTree.topologyRationale: A round solid of revolution at 14 segments. It is genuinely axially symmetric, unlike the roof it sits on, and it is gilt where the roof is timber - a separate material, so it cannot fold into the roof profile however well the axes line up. MACRO rather than meso despite being an ornament: it is the top 12% of the silhouette and it is what makes the declared 6.00 m height, so a blockout without it is measured against a reference 12% taller than itself.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Stepped base at the apex, a swelling bulb, a tapering needle, a collar and a ball terminal at exactly y=6.00, which is the declared height.

destruction.notes: Static landmark geometry; the asset declares no destruction groups, so no component carries a fractureGroup.

surfaceDetail.notes: Turned steps, bulb and collar in the lathe profile; polished gold leaf has no micro-relief, measured at heightP90Gradient 0.01709, the lowest of the four materials by a factor of four.

componentTree.name: Seated four-armed deity figure, body and lap
componentTree.topologyRationale: A solid of revolution at 10 segments. Reported at confidence 0.55.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Broad lap over crossed legs at the pedestal top, drawing in to a waist at y=2.40, swelling to a shoulder line at y=2.88 and closing to the neck at y=3.02.
geometryDescriptor.approximationNote: The four arms are NOT modelled: they are occluded by garland masses in the single plate, so there is no evidence for their number or gesture (unknown unk-deity-arms, confidence 0.3). The first build authored garlands over exactly the shoulder region that hides them, which masked the omission; the garlands were removed after review because displaced spheres read as orange blobs rather than flowers, so the bare shoulder now shows. A stated omission, not an oversight.

colorMaterialRecipe.notes: Gold leaf, same material as the columns and finial -- one shader switch for every gilt surface on the prop.

surfaceDetail.notes: Cast and gilded, faceted at 8 lathe segments so the figure reads as a cast sculpture rather than a turned vase. No surface relief, and since the garlands were removed nothing stands in front of it: the faceting is the whole of the figure's local detail.

componentTree.name: Four-faced head block and tiered crown
componentTree.topologyRationale: A square solid of revolution at segments=4 - and here the square is the ICONOGRAPHY, not a budget trick: four segments give the head block exactly four flat faces at 90 deg, which is what a Brahma image is. The 45 deg Y rotation puts one face on +Z, facing the street.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Neck, the four-faced head block from y=3.14 to y=3.40, then the tiered crown stepping in to a spire at y=3.88. Facial relief is not modelled: at prop distance on a low-end target the gilt response carries the read, and only one of the four faces is legible in the plate.

destruction.notes: Static landmark geometry; the asset declares no destruction groups, so no component carries a fractureGroup.

localFeatures.description: The head block from y=3.14 to 3.40 built at lathe segments=4, so it has exactly four flat faces at 90 degrees. Here the square is the iconography, not a budget trick.

surfaceDetail.notes: The crown tiers step in by 0.03 m each over a flared brow band -- built relief. The four faces are the four flat sides of a 4-segment lathe; facial features are NOT modelled and are the declared approximation.

Authored in plan (sx, sy) = (worldX, worldZ) and rotated -90 deg about X so the extrusion axis becomes world +Y.

geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: Four outline points and four hole points, one extrusion step: about 80 triangles including the reveal faces.
